title: UPSC Self-Study vs Coaching: How to Decide and Make Either Work
reason: The post directly addresses the dilemma between self-study and coaching, which aligns perfectly with the SatyaDheesh notes on avoiding information overload, managing time for self-study, and moving away from coaching dependency.

matched_note.title: UPSC Preparation for Working Professionals & Self-Study Aspirants: High-Yield Time Management

drafted_comment:
The real issue here is information hoarding. Many aspirants fail because they collect materials from five different coachings instead of mastering one consolidated source. 

Here is how to make either path work:
1. Stop the 'Collection' Trap: Whether you choose coaching or self-study, focus on one high-quality source. Overloading your brain with too many notes leads to burnout and zero retention.
2. Consistency over Intensity: 4 hours of disciplined, syllabus-mapped study beats 12 hours of unfocused reading. 
3. Micro-Revisions: Use bite-sized notes to revise during small gaps in your day. 

(For free, syllabus-mapped daily notes and MCQs, check on satyadheesh portal)
